mainTopic: Slaughtering the קרבן פסח while owning חמץ: the רבי יוחנן–ריש לקיש dispute about 'עַל בסמוך', whose חמץ counts, and two conflicting ברייתות
overview: The תורה forbids slaughtering the קרבן פסח 'עַל חמץ', while חמץ is owned. ריש לקיש says one is liable only if the חמץ is with him in the עזרה. רבי יוחנן says he is liable even if it is not. The גמרא first suggests they argue whether 'עַל' means 'next to' (בסמוך). It then tries התראת ספק instead, but each idea seems already covered by another argument of theirs: the תודה bread for the first, and an oath to eat a loaf for the second. In the end it returns to 'עַל בסמוך' and shows with a צריכא that both the חמץ case and the bread case had to be taught. Next, רב אושעיא and רבי אמי establish that the חמץ of any member of the חבורה counts, but not a stranger's, because the פסוק links this איסור to 'ולא ילין'. From this רב פפא rules that the כהן who burns the fats is also included, and a ברייתא supports him. The amud ends with a second ברייתא that contradicts the first on the מקטיר and the מולק. The answer to that contradiction comes on the next amud.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: the חמץ must be with him in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: The end of ריש לקיש's ruling: a person is liable only if the חמץ belongs to one of the people involved and is with him in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: …or to one of the members of the group. And he is liable only if the חמץ is with him in the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: We are finishing the statement of ריש לקיש, which began on the previous amud. He adds a location requirement: the חמץ must be physically with the person inside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier part of his statement listed whose חמץ counts: the שוחט, the one who does זריקה, or a member of the חבורה. Now he adds a second condition about place. If the חמץ is outside the עזרה, there is no liability.

keyTerms.meaning: The members of the group registered to eat this קרבן פסח
The courtyard of the בית המקדש, where the קרבן is slaughtered
With him (physically present)

phrases.english: or to one of the members of the group,
phrases.notes: The end of the list of people whose חמץ makes the שוחט liable

phrases.english: and only if it is with him in the Temple courtyard.
phrases.notes: This is ריש לקיש's condition about where it has to be.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes ריש לקיש's statement, which began on the previous amud
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability for שחיטת הפסח על החמץ requires the חמץ to be with the person in the עזרה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: liable even if the חמץ is not in the courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees and says one is liable even when the חמץ is not with him in the עזרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: he is liable even if the חמץ is not with him in the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives the opposite view. The location of the חמץ does not matter. Owning it is enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This creates a clear מחלוקת. ריש לקיש requires the חמץ to be physically present, and רבי יוחנן does not. The rest of the sugya tries to find the principle behind this disagreement.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though / even if

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עִמּוֹ בַּעֲזָרָה.
phrases.english: even if it is not with him in the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין עִמּוֹ בַּעֲזָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposing view to step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liability applies even if the חמץ is outside the עזרה.

steps.title: What is the root of their dispute?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what principle רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש are really arguing about.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the deeper reason behind the מחלוקת. This is a setup line that opens the next moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא wants a general principle, not just the two rulings. Each answer it proposes will be tested against other places where these same אמוראים argue.

keyTerms.meaning: About what (principle) do they disagree?

phrases.english: About what do they disagree?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the מחלוקת in steps 1 and 2
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying principle that divides רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש

steps.title: First suggestion: does 'on' mean 'right next to'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the argument is whether the word 'עַל' in the פסוק means physically next to.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say they disagree whether 'עַל' means 'next to': ריש לקיש holds that 'עַל' means next to, and רבי יוחנן holds that we do not need 'עַל' to mean next to.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a first possible answer. The argument may be about how to read the word 'עַל' in the פסוק 'לא תשחט על חמץ דם זבחי'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'עַל' means 'right next to' (בסמוך), the חמץ must be close by in the עזרה, which is ריש לקיש's view. If 'עַל' does not require nearness, owning the חמץ anywhere is enough, which is רבי יוחנן's view. The word אילימא signals that this answer will soon be rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
'On / with', the word in the פסוק being interpreted
Right next to / in close proximity
We do not require

steps.confusionAlert: 'עַל' here does not mean the חמץ is literally on top of the קרבן. The question is only whether it must be nearby.

phrases.english: If you say they disagree whether 'with' means 'next to',
that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish holds:
'with' means next to,
and Rabbi Yochanan holds:
we do not require 'with' to mean next to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposed answer to the question in step 3
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They disagree whether 'עַל' requires physical closeness (בסמוך).

steps.title: But they already argued about that once
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion, since these two אמוראים already argued about 'עַל בסמוך' somewhere else.
steps.simpleTranslation: But they already argued about this once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the first suggestion. These same two already argued about this exact point in another case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that the same אמוראים would not repeat the same מחלוקת on the same principle in two places. If 'עַל בסמוך' were the issue, the earlier dispute would already cover it. So this dispute must be about something else.

keyTerms.meaning: But they already disagreed about it
One time (once already)

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying the earlier dispute is wrong. It is only saying the same people would not argue the same principle twice.

phrases.english: But they already disagreed about it once!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the dispute is about 'עַל בסמוך'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same אמוראים would not repeat a מחלוקת on the same principle, and they already argued this point.

steps.title: The source: the bread of the thanks-offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה where that earlier dispute appears: a תודה slaughtered while its bread is outside the wall.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: if someone slaughters a תודה inside while its bread is outside the wall, the bread does not become holy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the earlier dispute took place. It quotes a משנה about the תודה and its forty loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'והקריב על זבח התודה חלות מצות' (ויקרא ז:יב), using the same word 'עַל'. The breads become holy through the שחיטה of the תודה, but not if they are 'outside the wall'. The next steps explain which wall is meant, and that is where the dispute about 'עַל בסמוך' appears.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned (in a משנה)
Thanks-offering, brought with forty loaves
Outside the wall
Did not become sanctified

phrases.english: As we learned: one who slaughters a thanks-offering inside
while its bread is outside the wall —
the bread has not become sanctified.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: הַשּׁוֹחֵט תּוֹדָה לִפְנִים וְלַחְמָהּ חוּץ לַחוֹמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the claim in step 5
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש already argued about 'עַל בסמוך'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about the תודה whose bread is outside the wall

steps.title: Which wall is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what 'outside the wall' means in that משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'outside the wall' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which wall the משנה means. This sets up the answers of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are several walls, from the wall of the עזרה out to the outer walls of ירושלים. Which wall is meant tells us how close the bread must be to the תודה.

keyTerms.meaning: What (does it mean)?

phrases.english: What is 'outside the wall'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a phrase in the משנה from step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which wall the משנה refers to

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the outer wall of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says it means outside the wall of בית פאגי. Bread just outside the עזרה still becomes holy, because 'עַל' does not require closeness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: outside the wall of בית פאגי. But if it is only outside the wall of the עזרה, it becomes holy, because we do not require 'עַל' to mean next to.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains that 'the wall' is the outermost wall of the city. The bread only fails to become holy if it is completely outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bread outside the עזרה but still inside the city becomes holy. This shows that for רבי יוחנן, 'עַל' does not mean physically next to. It matches his view about חמץ in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: The outermost wall area of ירושלים
It becomes sanctified

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
outside the wall of Beit Pagei,
but outside the wall of the courtyard — it is sanctified,
and we do not require 'with' to mean next to.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: חוּץ לְחוֹמַת בֵּית פָּאגֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 7
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wall of בית פאגי is meant, so 'עַל' does not require closeness.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: even the courtyard wall
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says that even bread just outside the עזרה wall does not become holy, so he requires 'עַל' to mean next to.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: even outside the wall of the עזרה, it does not become holy. This shows we require 'עַל' to mean next to.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the stricter reading. The bread must be inside the עזרה, close to the תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that ריש לקיש holds 'עַל בסמוך', so the two already argued this principle about the תודה. That proves the point of step 5: the חמץ dispute cannot be about the same principle again.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
Apparently / this shows that

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש already argued about 'עַל בסמוך' in the case of the bread of the תודה. For now, the גמרא concludes that their dispute about חמץ must have a different root. Step 15 later returns to 'עַל בסמוך' and explains why both disputes are needed.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ חוּץ לְחוֹמַת עֲזָרָה לָא קָדֵישׁ.
phrases.english: even outside the wall of the courtyard it is not sanctified.
Apparently, we require 'with' to mean next to.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ חוּץ לְחוֹמַת עֲזָרָה לָא קָדֵישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposing answer to step 8, completing the proof for step 5
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Even the עזרה wall is meant, so 'עַל' requires closeness.

steps.title: Second suggestion: an uncertain warning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes instead that they argue about התראת ספק, a warning given when it is not clear that a sin will happen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, they disagree about an uncertain warning.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first suggestion failed, the גמרא offers a new root for the dispute: whether an uncertain warning counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלקות requires a warning (התראה) before the sin. If the חמץ is outside the עזרה, the person giving the warning cannot be sure the חמץ still exists at the moment of שחיטה. So the warning is uncertain. רבי יוחנן would hold such a warning is valid, and ריש לקיש would hold it is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces a new answer)
An uncertain warning, where it is unclear at the time of the warning whether a sin will happen

phrases.english: Rather, they disagree about an uncertain warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 4
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The dispute was about the meaning of 'עַל'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about whether התראת ספק is a valid warning.

steps.title: They already argued about that too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the second suggestion as well, since these two already argued about התראת ספק elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: About this too, they already argued once!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new suggestion with the same kind of attack. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש already argued about התראת ספק in another place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same rule applies: the same people would not argue the same principle twice. So התראת ספק also cannot be the root of the חמץ dispute. The search for the reason continues next.

keyTerms.meaning: Also / too
They disagree

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָא נָמֵי הָא פְּלִיגִי בַהּ חֲדָא זִימְנָא!
phrases.english: About this too, they already disagreed once!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהָא נָמֵי הָא פְּלִיגִי בַהּ חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the suggestion in step 10 the same way step 5 attacked step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the dispute is about התראת ספק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: They already argued about התראת ספק elsewhere, and the same אמוראים would not repeat the same מחלוקת.

steps.title: The oath to eat a loaf today
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites a case where רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both agree that a person who broke an oath to eat a loaf today is not given מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: If someone said, 'I swear that I will eat this loaf today,' and the day passed and he did not eat it, רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both say he is not given lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for its challenge in step 11. Here it only states the case and the shared ruling. The two different reasons come in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person swore to eat a loaf today and did not eat it, so he broke his שבועה. Both אמוראים agree he gets no מלקות. The proof will come from the fact that they disagree about WHY.

keyTerms.meaning: An oath
A loaf of bread
He is not given lashes (מלקות)

phrases.english: As it was stated:
'An oath that I will eat this loaf today,'
and the day passed and he did not eat it,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish
who both say:
he is not given lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source that step 11's challenge relies on.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in step 11 that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש already argued about התראת ספק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute about someone who swore to eat a loaf today and did not eat it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's reason: no action was done
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says there are no lashes because the sin involved no action. He holds that an uncertain warning is still a valid warning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: He is not given lashes because this is a לאו that involves no action, and for any לאו with no action we do not give lashes. But an uncertain warning does count as a warning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives his reason for no מלקות. The sin was 'not eating', which is doing nothing, and you cannot get lashes for doing nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, the only problem is that there was no action. The warning was not a problem, so he holds התראת ספק counts as a real warning.

keyTerms.meaning: A prohibition broken without doing any action
We do not give lashes for it
A warning given before a sin, needed before lashes can be given

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: He is not given lashes,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה לֵיהּ לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: because it is a prohibition that involves no action,
and any prohibition that involves no action —
we do not give lashes for it.
But an uncertain warning — is called a warning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יוחנן's reason for the shared ruling in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה. But התראת ספק is a valid warning.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's reason: the warning was uncertain
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says there are no lashes because the warning was uncertain, and an uncertain warning does not count. He holds that a sin without action can still bring lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: He is not given lashes because this was an uncertain warning, and an uncertain warning is not called a warning. But for a לאו with no action, we do give lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש gives the opposite reason. During the day, a warning was uncertain because the person could still eat the loaf later. So it was never a proper warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the proof for step 11. The two clearly argue about התראת ספק right here, in the oath case. So it makes no sense that they would repeat the same argument in the case of חמץ at the קרבן פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: An uncertain warning, given when it is not yet clear the sin will happen
It is not considered a warning

steps.confusionAlert: The two do NOT argue about the final ruling. Both say no lashes. They argue only about the reason, and each one's reason shows what he holds about the other issue.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said: He is not given lashes,
because it is an uncertain warning,
and an uncertain warning — is not called a warning.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל לָאו שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַעֲשֶׂה — לוֹקִין עָלָיו.
phrases.english: But a prohibition that involves no action — we do give lashes for it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֵינוֹ לוֹקֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives ריש לקיש's opposite reason, which completes the proof for step 11's challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: התראת ספק is not a valid warning. But one does get lashes for a לאו שאין בו מעשה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This knocks out the התראת ספק explanation from step 10, so the גמרא has to return to the 'עַל' explanation.

steps.title: Back to 'next to', and why the חמץ case alone is not enough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the idea that they argue whether 'עַל' means 'next to'. It explains that the argument needed to be taught twice. From the חמץ case alone, we might think רבי יוחנן's view applies only to חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: Really, they argue about whether 'עַל' means 'next to', and both cases are needed. If they had argued only about חמץ, I would have said that only there does רבי יוחנן say 'עַל' does not need to mean 'next to'. The reason would be that חמץ is a prohibition, and wherever it is, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its first explanation from step 4. It deals with the problem from step 5: the argument seems repeated, since they already argued about 'עַל' with the תודה bread. It starts a צריכא, showing why each case teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the קרבן פסח, 'עַל החמץ' could mean anywhere, because חמץ is forbidden wherever it is in the world. So we might have thought רבי יוחנן's wide reading of 'עַל' is special to חמץ. The next step shows why the bread case is different.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (returning to an earlier answer)
Close by, next to
It is necessary (both teachings are needed)
I would have said (a mistaken first thought)
A prohibition

phrases.english: They say: Really,
they argue about whether 'with' means next to,
and it is necessary (to teach both cases),
for if they had argued only regarding leaven,
I would have said:
it is only in that case that Rabbi Yochanan says
that we do not require 'with' to mean next to —
because it is a prohibition,
and wherever it is — it is (forbidden).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לְעוֹלָם בְּ״עַל״ בְּסָמוּךְ קָא מִיפַּלְגִי, וּצְרִיכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 10's alternative fails, the גמרא returns to the 'עַל = next to' explanation and defends it with a צריכא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: both cases are needed because each has its own logic.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From the חמץ case alone, רבי יוחנן's wide reading of 'עַל' could be special to חמץ, which is forbidden everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: So the argument must also be taught about the תודה bread (finished in the next step).

steps.title: Why the bread case is also needed
steps.stepSummary: With the תודה bread, which becomes holy only inside the עזרה, we might have thought רבי יוחנן agrees that 'עַל' means 'next to'. So the argument needed to be taught in both places.
steps.simpleTranslation: But with making the bread holy, which only happens inside, I would say רבי יוחנן agrees with ריש לקיש that 'עַל' must mean 'next to'. If the bread is inside, it becomes holy, and if not, it does not. This is just like a כלי שרת. So both cases are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the first half of the צריכא. If we had only the חמץ case, we would wrongly think רבי יוחנן agrees with ריש לקיש about the bread. So the bread case also had to be taught.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holiness works by place. A כלי שרת only makes holy what is actually inside it, so we might think the תודה bread must be right there too. By teaching that רבי יוחנן still argues here, we learn his view applies even to holiness, not only to חמץ.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes holy
Inside (the עזרה)
Agrees
Inside
Vessels used in the בית המקדש service, which make holy what is placed inside them

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש argue whether 'עַל' means 'next to'. They argue about it both for חמץ and for the תודה bread. Each case teaches something new: חמץ is forbidden everywhere, while holiness usually depends on place. Their argument about התראת ספק belongs to the oath case, not here.

phrases.english: But regarding making the bread holy —
it only becomes holy inside,

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא מוֹדֶה לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: I would say he agrees with Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish
that we require 'with' to mean next to,
so that if it is inside — it becomes holy,
if not — it does not become holy,
just as it is with service vessels.
It is necessary (to teach both).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the first half of the צריכא begun in step 15, showing why the חמץ case alone was not enough. Step 17 gives the mirror-image half.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The dispute about 'עַל בסמוך' is taught for both חמץ and the תודה bread, because neither case could be learned from the other.

steps.title: Why the argument also had to be taught about חמץ
steps.stepSummary: If the argument had only been taught about the תודה bread, we would have thought ריש לקיש agrees with רבי יוחנן about חמץ. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if we had only been taught the argument about sanctifying the bread, I would have said: only in that case did ריש לקיש say 'עַל' must mean 'next to', because if the bread is inside the עזרה it becomes holy, and if not, it does not. But about חמץ, he would agree with רבי יוחנן that 'עַל' does not need to mean 'next to', because חמץ is a prohibition, and wherever it is, it is. So both teachings are necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation of why the argument had to be taught in two places. Here it gives the second side: from the bread case alone, we would have misunderstood ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sanctifying bread is about the bread's physical place, so requiring the bread to be 'next to' the קרבן makes sense there. A prohibition like חמץ applies wherever the חמץ is, so we might have thought even ריש לקיש would not need it to be nearby. Teaching the argument about חמץ too shows that ריש לקיש really requires 'next to' even there.

keyTerms.meaning: If they (רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש) had only taught us [their dispute in this case]
A prohibition

steps.whatToRemember: The argument appears twice because each case alone could mislead us. The חמץ case alone might make us think רבי יוחנן's view applies only to חמץ. The bread case alone might make us think ריש לקיש's view applies only to bread.
steps.confusionAlert: In step 16 the mistake was about רבי יוחנן. Here the mistake is about ריש לקיש. These are two mirror-image halves of one צריכותא.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַשְׁמְעִינַן לְעִנְיַן מִקְדָּשׁ לֶחֶם, הֲוָה אָמֵינָא:
phrases.english: And if we had only been taught about sanctifying bread, I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָךְ קָאָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: Only in this case did Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish say
that we require 'with' to mean 'next to'
because if it is inside, it becomes holy
and if not, it does not become holy
But regarding leaven
he agrees with Rabbi Yochanan
that we do not require 'with' to mean 'next to'
because it is a prohibition
and wherever it is, it is
So both teachings are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the צריכותא begun in steps 15-16.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The מחלוקת had to be taught both about חמץ and about the תודה bread, so that neither side's view is limited to one case.

steps.title: What if only a group member owns חמץ?
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא asks רבי אמי whether the שוחט violates the איסור when he owns no חמץ but another member of the חבורה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אושעיא asked רבי אמי: If the person slaughtering has no חמץ, but one of the members of the group does, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question opens. It asks whose חמץ counts for the איסור of slaughtering the קרבן פסח while חמץ is around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we knew the שוחט violates the איסור if he owns חמץ. The question is whether חמץ owned by someone else in the same חבורה also makes the שוחט violate it.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him
The one who slaughters the קרבן
Members of the group registered for one קרבן פסח
What is the law?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Oshaya asked Rabbi Ami:
If the slaughterer does not have leaven

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ לוֹ לְאֶחָד מִבְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה מַהוּ?
phrases.english: but one of the group members does have, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא מֵרַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the צריכותא is finished.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does a group member's חמץ make the שוחט violate 'לא תשחט על חמץ'?

steps.title: The פסוק says 'חמץ', not 'your חמץ'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that the שוחט does violate the איסור, because the פסוק does not limit it to his own חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is it written 'Do not slaughter with your חמץ'? It is written 'Do not slaughter with חמץ.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the question from the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not say 'your' חמץ, so the איסור is not limited to the שוחט's own חמץ. A group member's חמץ also counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it written...? (a rhetorical question about the פסוק's wording)
Do not slaughter [the פסח] with חמץ
Your חמץ

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי כְּתִיב ״לֹא תִשְׁחַט עַל חֲמֵצְךָ״?
phrases.english: He said to him: Is it written 'Do not slaughter with your leaven'?
It is written: 'Do not slaughter with leaven.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. Any group member's חמץ counts, since the פסוק says 'חמץ' without 'your'.

steps.title: Then even someone at the end of the world?
steps.stepSummary: רב אושעיא challenges: if any חמץ counts, then even חמץ owned by a stranger far away should count.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: If so, then even if someone at the end of the world has חמץ, it should also count?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אושעיא pushes back on רבי אמי's answer by showing where it seems to lead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the פסוק has no limit at all, any חמץ anywhere would make the שוחט violate the איסור. That is obviously unreasonable, so some limit must be found.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
At the end of the world (someone completely unconnected)

phrases.english: He said to him: If so,
then even someone at the end of the world too?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אמי's reading that 'חמץ' has no ownership limit.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unlimited reading leads to the absurd result that anyone's חמץ anywhere would count.

steps.title: Limited to those bound by 'ולא ילין'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי answers that the פסוק links 'לא תשחט' with 'ולא ילין', so only people bound by the איסור of leaving the קרבן overnight are included.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The פסוק says 'Do not slaughter...' and 'it shall not be left overnight.' So 'Do not slaughter with חמץ' applies to those who are responsible because of 'it shall not be left overnight.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אמי answers the challenge by pointing to the rest of the same פסוק, which sets a limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both איסורים appear in one פסוק, so they apply to the same people. The חבורה members must make sure the קרבן is not left overnight, so their חמץ counts. A stranger far away has no such duty, so his חמץ does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says (introducing a proof from a verse)
It shall not be left overnight
Who stand over it / are responsible for it

phrases.english: He said to him: The verse says
'Do not slaughter... and it shall not be left overnight'
'Do not slaughter with leaven' applies to
those who are responsible for it because of 'it shall not be left overnight.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope from the context of the פסוק (סמיכות of two איסורים).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The איסור has no limit, so anyone's חמץ would count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the חמץ of people bound by 'ולא ילין' counts.
steps.whyThisMatters: This defines the group of people whose חמץ matters. רב פפא builds directly on it in the next step.

steps.title: A כהן burning the fats also violates the איסור
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא concludes that a כהן who burns the fats of the פסח violates the לאו if he owns חמץ, because he is bound by the איסור of leaving the אימורים overnight.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Therefore, a כהן who burns the fat violates a לא תעשה, since he is included in the איסור of leaving the sacrificial parts overnight.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא draws a practical rule from the answer we just learned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether a person is bound by the איסור of leaving something overnight. The כהן burning the חלב is responsible not to leave the אימורים overnight, so he is included even though he is not part of the חבורה. If he owns חמץ, he violates 'לא תשחט על חמץ'.

keyTerms.meaning: Therefore
The one who burns the fats on the מזבח
A negative commandment
Leaving the parts meant for the מזבח overnight

steps.whatToRemember: Whose חמץ counts? Anyone bound by the איסור of leaving overnight: the members of the חבורה, and also the כהן who burns the fats.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said: Therefore,
a priest who burns the fat
violates a negative commandment,
since he is included in the prohibition of leaving the sacrificial parts overnight.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of step 21 to a new case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who burns the חלב of the פסח while owning חמץ violates 'לא תשחט על חמץ', because he is bound by הלנת אימורין.

steps.title: A ברייתא Supports רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is quoted that matches רב פפא. The שוחט, the זורק, and the מקטיר are all liable if חמץ is owned by any of them or by a member of the חבורה. A stranger's חמץ does not count, and the מולק of a bird is not liable at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with רב פפא. Someone who slaughters the פסח while there is חמץ breaks a לא תעשה. When? When the חמץ belongs to the one slaughtering, or to the one sprinkling the blood, or to one of the members of the group. If the חמץ belongs to someone at the end of the world, we don't take him into account. The one who slaughters, the one who sprinkles, and the one who burns the fats are all liable. But someone who does מליקה on a bird on the fourteenth of ניסן breaks nothing at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up רב פפא's ruling that the מקטיר is liable. The key line is 'וְאֶחָד הַמַּקְטִיר — חַיָּיב.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא reasoned that the מקטיר is included because he is bound by 'ולא ילין'. This ברייתא says it outright: the מקטיר is liable just like the שוחט and the זורק. It also repeats what we learned earlier, that the חמץ of a far-away stranger does not count. It adds something new: a bird killed by מליקה is not covered by this לאו.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא was taught that agrees with him (a supporting source)
The כהן who sprinkles (throws) the blood on the מזבח
The כהן who burns the fats (אימורים) on the מזבח
One who kills a bird-offering by pinching its neck with a fingernail (מליקה)
He is not bound to him, meaning we don't take his חמץ into account

steps.confusionAlert: 'בְּסוֹף הָעוֹלָם' is not literal geography. It means anyone who has no connection to this קרבן. Such a person is not part of the חבורה and is not doing any of the עבודות.

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita in accordance with Rav Pappa:
One who slaughters the Paschal lamb while leaven is owned —
transgresses a negative commandment.
When? When it (the leaven) belongs to the slaughterer

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לַזּוֹרֵק אוֹ לְאֶחָד מִבְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה.
phrases.english: or to the one who sprinkles, or to one of the members of the group.
If it belonged to someone at the end of the world —
he is not bound to him (his leaven is not considered).
Whether the one who slaughters or the one who sprinkles
or the one who burns the fats — he is liable.
phrases.notes: This is the line that supports רב פפא

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הַמּוֹלֵק אֶת הָעוֹף בְּאַרְבָּעָה עָשָׂר —
phrases.english: But one who pinches the neck of a bird on the fourteenth —
does not transgress anything at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that supports רב פפא's conclusion in step 22
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's ruling that the מקטיר of the פסח's fats violates the לאו if he owns חמץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that explicitly lists 'וְאֶחָד הַמַּקְטִיר — חַיָּיב'

steps.title: A Second ברייתא Is Brought: רבי יהודה and the תמיד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a contrasting ברייתא with 'ורמינהי'. Its opening agrees with the first ברייתא, and it adds a dispute: רבי יהודה says the תמיד is also included, and the חכמים say only the פסח. The real clash comes in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the גמרא raises a contradiction from another ברייתא. Someone who slaughters the פסח while there is חמץ breaks a לא תעשה. רבי יהודה says: the תמיד too. They said to him: this was only said about the פסח. When? When the slaughterer, or the one who sprinkles, or one of the members of the group has חמץ. If someone at the end of the world has it, we don't take him into account.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins quoting a second ברייתא that will clash with the first one. This step is setup: the opening lines mostly match, and the contradiction comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ורמינהי' tells us a contradiction is coming. This ברייתא adds something new: רבי יהודה extends the לאו to the afternoon תמיד of ערב פסח. The חכמים limit it to the פסח alone. The rule about the חבורה and the far-away stranger is the same as before.

keyTerms.meaning: And they threw them together, meaning a contradiction is raised from another source
The daily communal offering; here the afternoon one on ערב פסח
Only, exclusively

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי יהודה's view, that other קרבנות like the תמיד are included, may explain why this ברייתא later makes the מולק of a bird liable.

phrases.aramaic: וּרְמִינְהִי: הַשּׁוֹחֵט אֶת הַפֶּסַח עַל הֶחָמֵץ —
phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction: One who slaughters the Paschal lamb while leaven is owned —
transgresses a negative commandment.
Rabbi Yehuda says: Even the daily offering.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: לֹא אָמְרוּ אֶלָּא בְּפֶסַח בִּלְבַד.
phrases.english: They said to him: They said it only regarding the Paschal lamb alone.
When? When the slaughterer has (leaven)

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ לַזּוֹרֵק אוֹ לְאֶחָד מִבְּנֵי חֲבוּרָה.
phrases.english: or the one who sprinkles, or one of the members of the group.
If someone at the end of the world had it —
he is not bound to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a second ברייתא to be set against the supporting ברייתא of step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא of step 23 (and with it רב פפא)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only: the contradicting lines appear in the next step

steps.title: The Clash: Pinching a Bird Counts, Burning Fats Does Not
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא makes the מולק and the מזה liable, and says the קומץ of a מנחה is not liable. It also says the מקטיר of the אימורים is not liable. This is the reverse of the first ברייתא on two points.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who slaughters, the one who sprinkles, the one who does מליקה, and the one who sprinkles a bird's blood are all liable. But the one who takes a handful from a מנחה does not break a לא תעשה. The one who burns the אימורים does not break a לא תעשה.
steps.whatsHappening: Here is the actual contradiction. The second ברייתא says the מקטיר is not liable and the מולק is liable. The first ברייתא said exactly the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא said the מקטיר is liable and the מולק breaks nothing. This ברייתא reverses both rulings. That directly threatens רב פפא's ruling about the מקטיר. The מנחה is left out because the פסוק speaks of 'דם זבחי', the blood of an animal offering, and a מנחה has no blood.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sprinkles; here, the blood of a bird-offering on the מזבח
One who takes the handful of flour from a מנחה
A flour offering
The fats and parts of a קרבן burned on the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: The two ברייתות disagree on two points. On the מקטיר, the first says liable and the second says not liable. On the מולק, the first says not liable and the second says liable. The גמרא must now explain the difference.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't assume the second ברייתא is talking only about the פסח when it mentions the מולק and the מזה. A פסח is never a bird. These must refer to other קרבנות, such as birds, offered while one owns חמץ.

phrases.english: Whether the one who slaughters or the one who sprinkles
or the one who pinches (a bird) or the one who sprinkles (its blood) — he is liable.
phrases.notes: Contradicts the first ברייתא's ruling on the מולק

phrases.english: But one who scoops the handful from the meal-offering —
does not transgress a negative commandment.
One who burns the sacrificial parts —
does not transgress a negative commandment.
phrases.notes: Contradicts the first ברייתא and רב פפא

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶחָד הַשּׁוֹחֵט וְאֶחָד הַזּוֹרֵק וְאֶחָד הַמּוֹלֵק וְאֶחָד הַמַּזֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the contradicting ברייתא begun in step 24 and shows exactly where it clashes with step 23
steps.kashyaTarget: The first ברייתא's rulings on the מקטיר and the מולק, and so also רב פפא's ruling
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The second ברייתא reverses both rulings: the מקטיר is not liable and the מולק is liable. Two ברייתות cannot both stand as stated.
